concept.name: Positive volume index
concept.definition: The complement of the Negative Volume Index: Dysart's cumulative index (in Fosback's formulation) that accumulates percentage price changes only on periods when volume increases, tracking what the volume-driven 'crowd' is doing.
concept.intuition: High-volume days are when the crowd trades; PVI isolates those days to show the crowd's cumulative net effect on price.
concept.mechanics: When today's volume exceeds yesterday's, add the percentage price change (scaled by the index) to the running PVI from a base of 1000; otherwise the index is unchanged. Watched against its 255-period (one-year) moving average: above it confirms rising prices, below it confirms declines.
concept.formula: If V_t > V_{t-1}: PVI_t = PVI_{t-1} + ((C_t - C_{t-1})/C_{t-1}) x PVI_{t-1}; else PVI_t = PVI_{t-1}.
concept.failure_modes: Prone to whipsaw crossovers of its moving average, and it can fall while price rises strongly if the biggest-volume days are down days; the crowd-is-wrong premise is a heuristic, not an established fact.
concept.misconceptions: Fosback's 67%/21% bear-market odds are period-specific historical results, and PVI above its one-year average 'confirms' rather than predicts a price rise.
concept.example: From PVI 1000: volume jumps and price rises 1.2%, so PVI = 1012; next day volume falls and price drops 0.5%, and PVI stays 1012.
